name: Banned Python patterns for engineer agents and reviews
short_definition: Canonical banned-pattern catalog for Python services in the engineer stack as of 2026-07-13: packaging, typing, async, FastAPI, auth, data, workers, testing, and deploy anti-patterns that agents must not generate and reviewers must flag. Aggregates anti_patterns + deprecation_watch from all researched py-* leaves into a single scan-oriented list with severity and remediation.
scope_in: Banned patterns by cluster with severity (blocker/major/minor)
Cross-stack mirrors of TS/Rust anti-patterns (any↔Any, unwrap↔bare except)
scope_out: Style nits already covered by ruff defaults without policy weight
Framework bugs unrelated to agent/codegen choices

severity_model.blocker: Must not merge / agent must not emit — security, data loss, or wrong stack default
severity_model.major: Fix before ship of feature; allowed only with migration ticket

defaults.response_to_hit: Replace with blessed alternative from py-default-stack-snapshot + leaf item; do not dual-stack

use_when: Code review, engineer audit, agent output validation
Writing scan rules or pre-commit bans
do_not_use_when: Third-party vendor code vendored as-is (isolate; don't 'fix' inside vendor)
alternatives: Leaf anti_patterns fields for deeper rationale

do: Treat blocker list as hard gate in greenfield
Document temporary exceptions with ticket + expiry
Align bans with PY-* scan IDs from py-agent-codegen-rules
Mirror TS anti-patterns culture (no any, validate at boundary)
dont: Don't 'allow until broken' on auth/SSRF/secret patterns
Don't add a second formatter/typechecker to silence a ban
Don't copy Django/Flask tutorial patterns into FastAPI async services blindly
Don't weaken requires-python or skip lock to make a banned dep install

code_skeleton:
# Banned → Blessed (quick map)

# Packaging
# BAD: poetry init / pip freeze > requirements.txt as sole truth
# GOOD: uv init; uv add; commit uv.lock

# Format/lint
# BAD: black + isort + flake8
# GOOD: ruff format + ruff check

# Types
# BAD: mypy-only greenfield; typing.List; Any everywhere
# GOOD: basedpyright CI; list[str]; X | None; Protocol

# FastAPI lifecycle
# BAD: @app.on_event("startup"); global engine = create_async_engine(...) at import
# GOOD: lifespan; engines on app.state; dispose on exit

# Auth
# BAD: from jose import jwt; jwt.decode(token, key)  # no algorithms
# GOOD: import jwt; jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=["RS256"], audience=..., issuer=...)

# Async
# BAD: requests.get(...); time.sleep(1) in async def
# GOOD: await client.get(...); await asyncio.sleep(1)

# Jobs
# BAD: background_tasks.add_task(capture_payment, ...)
# GOOD: await taskiq_broker.kick(capture_payment, ...)  # durable queue

# Data
# BAD: session.query(User).all(); response = orm_user
# GOOD: (await session.scalars(select(User).where(...))).all(); UserOut.model_validate(row)

# CORS
# BAD: allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True
# GOOD: allow_origins=settings.cors_origins  # explicit list
failure_modes: Async blocking anti-patterns → event-loop stalls under load
Pool/pooler anti-patterns → connection exhaustion and 500 storms
Dual migrations → RLS drift and broken deploys

anti_patterns.remediation: basedpyright CI; mypy only for legacy plugins

anti_patterns.pattern: Hardcoded secrets / service_role in client paths
Public models allow extra fields by default
Lazy load after await / N+1 loops
Alembic + Supabase both owning same tables
New arq systems without maintenance note
SQLite as Postgres stand-in for PG apps
msgspec default for all HTTP models

versions_as_of.note: Bans are version-stable; re-verify tool-specific bans (arq maintenance, ty beta, uv audit preview) by review_by
versions_as_of.python-jose: avoid greenfield regardless of 3.5.0 on PyPI
versions_as_of.ty: 0.0.x beta — ban as sole CI gate

config_snippets.grep_blockers:
# quick local greps (also automate as PY-*)
rg -n 'from jose import|@app\\.on_event|session\\.query\\(|parse_obj|\\.dict\\(\\)|--reload' services packages
rg -n 'allow_origins\\s*=\\s*\\[\\s*[\"']\\*[\"']' services
rg -n 'jwt\\.decode\\(' services -A2 | rg -v algorithms
rg -n 'BackgroundTasks' services | rg -i 'payment|stripe|transfer|webhook'

deprecation_watch: passlib as sole modern password stack without argon2/bcrypt care
Gunicorn assumed mandatory for all FastAPI
Floating git deps and requirements.txt-only apps
Safety/pip-audit as primary when uv audit available
ts_boundary: TS anti-patterns (any, client-only validation, getSession without server verify) mirror Python (Any, missing Pydantic, trusting JWT claims without verify). Keep bans aligned in spirit across typescript.md and python.md.
rust_boundary: Rust unwrap-in-handler ban ↔ Python bare except / str(e) to client. Don't replace Python anti-pattern piles by rewriting to Rust without fixing design.
supabase_boundary: Banned: service_role in browser; dual migration owners; RLS-off 'just for the Python service' without compensating authz. Python may use service role server-side with explicit filters — still not an excuse to skip ownership checks.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI must not document endpoints that skip auth without explicit public:true review
Error responses must not include stack traces (contract test / middleware check)
Migration files must not mix tools on same table names

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: Detect and ban unsafe/outdated Python patterns

threats: Auth bypass and alg confusion from jose/no-algorithms
Secret exfiltration via logs and committed .env

must_generate: When touching banned pattern, replace with blessed alternative in same PR when scope allows
Severity-tagged comments only for temporary exceptions with ticket
must_not_generate: Any blocker anti-pattern from this catalog in greenfield
Dual-stack 'compatibility' layers that preserve bans forever
Disabling ruff/typecheck to hide a ban

tests_required: Fixture corpus of banned snippets fails scanner
Chaos: kill worker mid-BackgroundTasks-equivalent critical path → proves durable path exists for money
ci_gates: engineer-scan --backend or Python mode including AP-* / PY-* blockers

positive: Blessed stack imports only (fastapi, pydantic, sqlalchemy, httpx, jwt, structlog)
Taskiq/Temporal for durable jobs with idempotency keys

skill_module_bullets: Anti-patterns section in references/python.md is a severity table (blocker/major/minor) with remediation — not a blog.

Blockers: Poetry greenfield, no lock, Black/flake8 stack, on_event, python-jose, jwt without algorithms, hardcoded secrets, requests-in-async, BackgroundTasks for money, dual migrations, create_all prod, CORS*+creds, --reload prod, pooler without mitigations, log secrets, infinite retries.
Majors: mypy-only greenfield, Any public APIs, thick handlers, create_task leaks, N+1/lazy async, ORM-as-JSON, arq new systems, msgspec-as-default, free-threading default, SQLite-as-Postgres tests.
Minors: typing.List/Optional, tutorial-only style issues already fixed by ruff UP/I.
Each ban maps to scan ID (AP-* / PY-*) and blessed alternative from default stack snapshot.
Mirror TS/Rust culture: validate at boundary, no silence compilers, no leak internals.
Brownfield: ticketed exceptions with expiry; do not normalize dual-tool forever.
Workers: pickle ban; infinite-retry ban; DLQ required for poison; no ack-then-forget for critical.
Data: SQL-first repos; no string-interpolated SQL; service_role still filters tenant in SQL.
Auth/SSRF: never open fetch; never trust client role alone; 401 vs 403 discipline.
Deprecation watch list separate from bans — tools that are outdated but may appear in old blogs (uWSGI, nest_asyncio, OAuth implicit).
Agent evals should include 'reject banned scaffold' cases for top 10 blockers.
action_items: Publish full AP-* table into references/python.md § Anti-patterns with columns: ID, Severity, Pattern, Remediation, Scan.
Implement automated detection for all blocker AP-* in engineer-scan; start with jose, on_event, session.query, --reload, CORS*+creds, parse_obj/.dict(), poetry.lock.
Add CONTRIBUTING or skill note: new bans require research leaf citation + review_by date.
Create tests/fixtures/banned/ corpus for scanner unit tests.
Cross-link each major ban to leaf research JSON for rationale depth.
In audit template, add Critical bucket pre-filled with blocker anti-pattern checks.
Train agent system prompt with top-15 blockers only (progressive disclosure); full table on-demand in python.md.
Schedule quarterly review of deprecation_watch (arq, ty, uv audit stability, Granian claims).
Align gitleaks + secret scanning with AP-AUTH-SECRETS and AP-OBS-SECRETS.
Document migration playbooks: Poetry→uv, Black→ruff, mypy→basedpyright, jose→PyJWT, Celery-keep vs Taskiq-new.
When py-docker-deploy research lands, add Docker root/--reload/health anti-patterns if not already covered.
Ensure typescript.md and rust.md anti-pattern sections cross-link python.md for polyglot PRs.
checklist: No blocker AP-* in changed Python files
Tests not using SQLite-as-Postgres for PG apps
conflicts_noted: Celery is banned as silent greenfield default but allowed when org-standard — severity major not blocker for presence alone
mypy banned as greenfield default but valid brownfield — scan should warn not always fail
Some communities still prefer aiohttp; stack standard is httpx — ban is 'default agent choice' not 'never use'
Granian is not banned; forcing it without measure is the anti-pattern
